title: @sohoplace & Marvellous - reviewed with photos
transcript: I am so excited I've just been to the first New West End theater to open in the last 50 years and to add to my excitement it's primarily a theater in the round the most intimate kind of theater there is I've just seen the first production to play in the space marvelous that's the name of the show whether it is marvelous I'll come to later but first a bit more about the building it's London inside the auditorium there are 602 seats you know the configuration is flexible but it was designed with theater in the round in mind and I hope we'll see lots more Productions using this Arrangement certainly marvelous and the next two Productions as you like it and Madea are in the round the sight lines are excellent I'm told no member of the audience will be more than six rows away looking for somewhere to eat so congratulations to Nico burns the owner of Soho place and her team for a terrific achievement such a welcome addition to London's West End on then to marvelous the story of Neil Baldwin based on his autobiography now you may have seen the bafta winning BBC film of the same name in which case you'll know about Neil A man with a learning disability who became an honorary graduate of Keel University a clown in a circus and kipman a mascot for Stoke City Football Club as well as many other honors including a British Empire medal thanks to his sheer determination helped by a happy disposition it not only recounts the major events of his life it does so in a way that reflects the anarchic approach of Neil himself the thing is thanks largely to his mother Neil has never accepted any limitations because of his disability simply goes and asks or sometimes goes without asking so he applies to be the manager of Stoke City well he doesn't get that job but he persists and is taken on by the appointed manager Lou Makari as someone who can and does Boost morale similarly he rolls up at Keel University where his mother works and starts welcoming students he's never formally employed there but he becomes an honorary member of the students union and 50 years later he's celebrated with an honorary degree despite his confidence there are moments when his disability is a cause for discrimination he's unpaid and treated badly by the circus owner but when he's bullied at school or later at work he takes it in his stride and gets his own back with a practical joke good work it's a form of theater that steps outside the restrictions of a formal stage play and makes the audience and the creation of the drama part of the show so from the start the actors gather to construct a play about Neil Baldwin and within minutes Neil or an actor playing the part of real Neil appears from the audience and becomes an active participant in its creation now this is interesting because Neil himself was involved in the making of this play and as we find out at the end the real real is actually present at each or I guess most performances sitting in the Stalls so he the character real Neil is consulted and increasingly involved in the play that is apparently being created before our eyes planned scenes are scrapped new interpretations introduced in keeping with his nature Neil is determined that there should be no serious stuff keep it happy seems to be his theme nearly all the actors are called upon at one stage or another to play Neil in indicating perhaps his many roles in life by the second act real Neil is playing himself and what a superb actor Michael Hugo is he mimics Neil's characteristically slow speech and offers his recognizable twinkling eyes and mischievous grin the other actors are also very talented and play a multitude of characters Alex Frost Gareth Cassidy Daniel Murphy and Shelly Atkinson who was standing in for Charlie bence kept us creased up with their multitude of accents and their physical comedy her Jerome Marsh Reed is a brilliant clown and has a breathtaking ability to fall crashing to the ground and Susan Ahmet is a commanding presence as Neil's mother the play is packed with Stage skills the slo-mo replays of football tackles are hilarious Neil has a Mary poppin style bag from which most of the props appear thanks to much activity under stage uh there are copious custard pies and other forms of slosh including spraying the audience with water and foam in fact audience participation is dariga the problem is the longer it goes on the play which is at first quick-witted and fast moving begins to try too hard to get laughs it's as if director Teresa heskins who also gets a co-writing credit with Malcolm Clark and of course Neil Baldwin is throwing everything in but the kitchen sink well actually there is a kitchen sink of sorts I was almost expecting a pantomime Dame to appear and in addition to the force fun it becomes by the end overly sentimental all of which meant I was less involved than I should have been behind the comedy there are some serious points about disability discrimination but also that disability need not be a barrier to achieving your dreams of course in the play and in the spirit of Neil Baldwin that will be a cue for another custom pie marvelous may not be a five-star play to open this five-star theater nevertheless it is a happy show about a happy man so if you're looking for a fun night out it's certainly worth a visit I give
